title: 4 in 10 UK Teens Want More Work Experience at School
paragraphs: Many teenagers in the UK want schools to do more to prepare them for the world of work, according to a new survey.
The survey was carried out by the research company Survation for the BBC. It asked 2,000 young people aged 13 to 18 about work and the support they need to find a job in the future.

When asked what kind of skills or guidance they would like more of at school, the most common answer was more work experience. About 44% of teenagers chose this. Work experience means spending time at a real workplace to learn what a job is like.

Many teenagers also want help with other practical skills. About 43% said they would like more help with managing money, and a similar number said they would like more guidance on how to apply for jobs.
The survey also showed that many young people have not had the chance to try work experience. More than half of the teenagers said they had never done any work experience.
As part of the project, the BBC also followed four students from Newcastle as they tried different work experience placements.
According to reports, the government in England wants to make sure that all secondary school students can get two weeks of work experience.

Other research shows why this may be important. A report by the charity Education and Employers, published in June 2026, found that young people who have the most contact with employers before the age of 16 are much less likely to end up without a job, education or training later. However, the report also found that teenagers from poorer families have fewer of these opportunities.
